editorial:
You follow Ray Gaines, a rescue helicopter pilot, as California gets torn apart by a massive earthquake. His estranged daughter Blake is trapped in San Francisco, and Ray teams up with his ex-wife Emma to reach her. The movie is loud, fast, and packed with collapsing buildings, tsunamis, and impossible escapes. You feel the ground shake as Los Angeles and San Francisco crumble, and the movie keeps moving from one rescue to the next. It is not subtle, but it knows exactly what kind of disaster ride it wants to be.

Dwayne Johnson brings steady charm, Carla Gugino adds heart, and Alexandra Daddario gives Blake real courage. The action is huge and easy to follow, though the science is silly and some family drama feels familiar. If you want a big, popcorn-style disaster movie, this delivers. It is a great pick for a weekend movie night with friends who enjoy big stunts and loud sound. Watch it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ray and Emma reach San Francisco after the tsunami and find Blake trapped in a collapsing building with Ben and Ollie. Ray pulls Blake from the water just in time, and the family reunites. They climb to higher ground as the city lies in ruins, and Ray promises they will rebuild together. The twist is that the disaster brings the broken family back together, turning a rescue mission into a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big disaster movies, Dwayne Johnson action, and loud popcorn entertainment.
